inputs.modified_text:
Look, what we are seeing unfold with this trial in PARIS, France is a textbook example of how the state weaponizes its coercive power to crush alternative communities and suppress non-conformity. Father Bernard Domini, the superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), has just been convicted under a deeply concerning and controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” This is a glaring window into systemic overreach and institutional failure.

When the establishment deploys these vague, heavy-handed legal tools under the guise of public safety, it inevitably targets vulnerable groups and criminalizes those who live outside the mainstream. Religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France are entirely justified in sounding the alarm over this dangerous precedent. Instead of addressing the actual root causes of inequality and institutional imbalance, the powers that be rely on subjective pretexts to crush basic freedoms and protect elite power structures at the expense of ordinary people. This case proves that we desperately need radical structural reform, not authoritarian laws.
